text:
Winnipeg went 3 for 4 on the power play, and that was the game. Cole Perfetti deflected one in at 13:04 of the first, Kyle Connor added a backhand 92 seconds later, and Connor's snap shot at 5:41 of the second made it 3-0. Those three goals came on chances worth 10, 7 and 28 percent. Detroit went 1 for 5 with the man advantage, despite creating 1.55 expected goals on those five chances.

Everything else belonged to Detroit. The Red Wings out-attempted Winnipeg 78 to 53 and led the expected-goals count 4.91 to 2.83, with an even-strength edge of 2.91 to 1.44. Over a full replay of every shot, Detroit wins this game 82 percent of the time. Stuart Skinner is the reason it didn't happen. He stopped 34 of 36 shots, and Detroit's chances were worth 4.91 expected goals against him, so he saved about 2.9 goals more than an average goalie would have. John Gibson, on the other side, was a shade below expectation (-0.37).

Detroit did claw back. Viktor Arvidsson deflected in a power-play goal at 16:52 of the second, and Emmitt Finnie scored at even strength 4:56 into the third, a 66 percent chance. The Red Wings then outchanced Winnipeg 1.58 to 0.50 in expected goals for the period, but couldn't find a third. Connor finished with two goals and an assist, Perfetti with a goal and two assists, and both looked like the right three stars.
